purpose: Structured record of what each of the nine provisioned scanner runners is, and the declared run-time input of the normalizer. harness/lib/normalize/paths.py consumes it (load_runner_metadata, ToolPathBase) and cannot resolve a single path without it; harness/lib/normalize/cli.py takes its path as an argument. oss-scan-results/tool-status.md is rendered FROM this file afterwards and is never an input to it.
provenance: Every value below was read from a provisioned file, measured by running a provisioned code path, or is null with an accompanying evidence string. No value is inferred from an artifact this pipeline produced, and no value is a guess.
spark_src_commit_evidence: git -C /opt/spark-src rev-parse HEAD printed 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d, which equals SPARK_SRC_COMMIT as exported by harness/env.sh line 44 and the pin named in harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 5.

definition_sites: harness/env.sh lines 87-89 - documented as setup-time verification only and deliberately NOT exported
harness/lib/scope.sh line 23 - scope_resolve_target takes the override branch when it is non-empty
harness/lib/scope.sh lines 25-27 - sets SCAN_ROOT to the override and marks SCAN_ROOT_SOURCE 'SETUP-TIME OVERRIDE - NOT A REAL SCAN'
harness/lib/scope.sh lines 43-48 - scope_dirs returns a single '.' instead of the allowlist expansion when it is set
smoke_override.evidence: Measured in a fresh non-login shell (env -i BLITZY_CLONE_INDEX=5 bash --noprofile --norc, then . harness/env.sh): ${HARNESS_SMOKE_TARGET:+SET}${HARNESS_SMOKE_TARGET:-unset} printed 'unset'. scope_resolve_target therefore took the SPARK_SRC branch at harness/lib/scope.sh lines 29-32 and scope_dirs returned the 18-directory allowlist expansion rather than '.'.
smoke_override.consequence_if_set: Every runner would be redirected at one small directory while still reporting success, so the run would silently scan the wrong thing.

path_base_kind_vocabulary.note: Closed set. Every tools.<tool>.path_base.kind below is one of these literals. A base that could not be established is the literal 'none' with an evidence string, never an empty string.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.scan_root: Emitted paths are relative to the SPARK_SRC scan root recorded in this document.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.per_target_directory: Emitted paths are relative to whichever of the several target paths the record came from, so the record's own root-relative or absolute sibling field named in path_base.anchor_fields is the anchor.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.filesystem_absolute: Emitted paths are absolute filesystem paths and must be relativized against the scan root.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.process_working_directory: Emitted paths are relative to the process working directory at invocation, which is distinct from the scan root only where the runner cds elsewhere.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.per_section_target: Emitted paths are relative to a per-section target inside the artifact rather than to any single root.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.bytecode_class: No filesystem path in the scanned tree is emitted; a class identifier must be resolved to a source path.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.absolute_targets: The runner passes absolute target paths, so emitted paths are absolute echoes of those targets.
path_base_kind_vocabulary.none: No explicit base could be established from the runner. paths.py must reject such a record under unresolvable_path rather than fall back.

gate_stage.description: Everything establishable by reading the provisioned harness, without any scan and without depending on the pinned clone: the harness/bin/ enumeration and classification, each runner's argument guard by inspection, each runner's scan-target variable, invocation form, working directory, baked flags, JDK export, interpreter, credential expression and artifact name.

environment_record_read_first.evidence: harness/ENVIRONMENT.md lines 6-10 instruct 'Source this file first, in a fresh non-login shell: . harness/env.sh'. That file was sourced under env -i bash --noprofile --norc and exited 0. The name was read from the record rather than assumed.

checks.check: harness/bin/ enumerated and every entry classified against the AAP section 0.5.4 scanner-class table
checks.detail: Nine entries, all runners, one per canonical tool identifier. No entry names a scanner the class table does not carry. No helper and no orchestrator exists.

checks.check: each runner's argument guard precedes any environment sourcing, target resolution or tool invocation, established by inspection
checks.detail: The guard is the first executable statement in all nine. Per-runner line numbers are in tools.<tool>.argument_guard. No rejection probe was run and none was permitted, because inspection settled the ordering.

checks.check: bash -n over all nine runners plus harness/env.sh and harness/lib/scope.sh
both artifact trees exist and are empty
checks.detail: harness/artifacts/raw and harness/artifacts/logs each held 0 entries at the moment of this check. They are created by the provisioned environment file itself - harness/env.sh line 91 runs mkdir -p on HARNESS_RAW_DIR, HARNESS_LOG_DIR and HARNESS_SCRATCH_DIR - and not by this run. They are absent from a fresh clone because .gitignore line 31 is 'artifacts/' and git cannot track an empty directory.

checks.check: the allowlist holds the twelve authoritative globs byte-exact
checks.detail: sha256 0013edf6cdc3a48d69aed5d7db41cc6647cfd461d348f5e1d563ba85664143d1 over harness/scope/allowlist.txt equals the expected value, so the file is REFERENCE state and was left exactly as found.

checks.check: the nine tools resolve on PATH and report their versions
checks.detail: Observed versions are recorded per tool in tools.<tool>.observed_version. All nine equal the expected pins.

checks.check: both JDKs present and their major versions confirmed
no credential is present that an unmodifiable runner would expose
checks.detail: All five variables any runner reads are absent, and every runner that prints one prints a fixed token through scope_cred_state, which uses ${VAR:+set} only. See credentials_observed below.

credentials_observed.note: Presence only, as booleans. No credential value is recorded anywhere in this document, and none is printed by any runner.

NVD_API_KEY.note: Leave unset rather than set to an empty string: Dependency-Check aborts on an empty key with 'Invalid API Key, length of 0 too short'.

BC_API_KEY.note: Checkov severities require a licence, so severity_native is absent from every checkov row in this configuration.

sonatype_oss_index.note: No variable is read; the analyzer is switched off explicitly by --disableOssIndex so that the disabling is this harness's and is recorded.

GITHUB_TOKEN.note: Present in the ambient environment for downloads only. Read by no runner and printed by none, so no runner can expose it and no halt arises. harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 13 states the same.

credentials_observed.unsafe_expression_form_evidence: The ${VAR:+set}${VAR:-absent} form - whose :- arm expands to the variable's own value when the variable is set - occurs in no executable expression in any runner or library. grep over harness/bin/run-*.sh and harness/lib/scope.sh finds credential reporting only through scope_cred_state, defined at harness/lib/scope.sh lines 105-109 as eval "_state=\${$1:+set}" followed by printf of exactly 'set' or 'absent'. The fragment ${VAR:-absent} does appear once as prose, in scope.sh's own warning comment at line 102 explaining why it is not used; that is documentation, not code, and it is named here so a reader who greps for it is not left thinking this record is wrong.

notes: harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 1 lists shellcheck among this image's absent tools, but /usr/bin/shellcheck is present and the clone instantiation instructions record shellcheck 0.10.0. This is a host-tooling observation rather than an inherited scanner or runner fact, both statements are recorded here, and it halts nothing.

harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 4 states 58 and 60 '--config directories' for opengrep and semgrep. That figure is the runner's own printed ${#CFG[@]}, which counts argv tokens at two per directory. The rule-bearing directory counts are 29 and 30, reproduced exactly by running each runner's own CFG loop. This is a difference of counting unit, not a contradicted fact, and both numbers are recorded per tool.
This run installs nothing, edits no runner and edits no baked flag. Every condition that would halt the run is recorded in the halts array rather than repaired.

stage1_finalisation.description: The half that cannot precede the pinned tree existing: the scan-target value in force, the root each runner actually resolves, and this file's finalisation. Completed before any scanning invocation.
stage1_finalisation.pinned_tree_origin: Provisioning had already cloned and built the pinned tree at /opt/spark-src, and the clone instantiation instructions forbid re-cloning it. The precondition of this half was therefore already satisfied, and this run verifies the tree's identity with git rev-parse HEAD instead of cloning it.
stage1_finalisation.scan_target_value_mechanism: harness/env.sh line 43 exports SPARK_SRC="${SPARK_SRC:-/opt/spark-src}", so sourcing the environment file puts the pinned path in force and any caller may override it without editing the file. Setting a variable a runner is written to consume is not runner reconfiguration; no runner file and no baked flag was touched.

resolved_scan_root_verification.method: Sourced harness/env.sh and harness/lib/scope.sh in a fresh non-login shell and called scope_resolve_target - the same function every one of the nine runners calls - then read SCAN_ROOT and SCAN_ROOT_SOURCE. No scanner was invoked and nothing was written to harness/artifacts/raw.
resolved_scan_root_verification.why_one_measurement_covers_nine: All nine runners resolve their target through this single function and none contains its own target logic, so the resolved root is identical for all nine by construction. Each runner's call site line number is recorded in tools.<tool>.argument_guard.first_target_resolution_line.

allowlist_expansion_observed.evidence: scope_dirs (harness/lib/scope.sh lines 40-62) expands the twelve globs under globstar, nullglob and dotglob with the trailing /** stripped, skips any path containing src/test, and sorts unique. Eighteen directories from twelve globs is arithmetic on the allowlist, not an extension of it: the allowlist stays byte-exact.

stage1_finalisation.targeting_fault_rule: A runner whose configuration, invocation or recorded path base showed it resolved a tree other than SPARK_SRC would halt the run, because every finding it produced would be about the wrong code. None did. This is strictly separate from an individual finding whose coordinate falls outside the tree, which is a legitimate coordinate retained with in_scope false.

harness_bin_inventory_summary.orchestrator_note: There is deliberately no orchestrator and no run-all.sh in this provisioning; harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 8 states that harness/bin/ contains exactly the nine runners and nothing else, on the ground that an orchestrator would destroy per-tool attribution and its continue-on-error sequencing would carry a run past a condition that must stop it. Had one existed it would have been classified and left alone with invoked_by_this_run false.
harness_bin_inventory_summary.non_runner_helpers_note: The harness's non-runner helpers live outside harness/bin/, in harness/lib/: scope.sh (the shared scope, logging and credential contract, sourced by all nine) and joern-scan.sc (the bounded Joern query set). Neither is a runner and neither is invoked directly.
harness_bin_inventory_summary.evidence: ls -la harness/bin/ returned exactly nine regular files, all mode 755, all named run-<tool>.sh, and each maps to one canonical tool identifier in the AAP section 0.5.4 class table.

halts_note: Empty because no halting condition was observed. The conditions checked, each of which would have been recorded here rather than repaired: an entry in harness/bin/ naming a scanner absent from the class table; fewer or more than nine runners; an argument guard sitting after any scanning step; a runner resolving a tree other than SPARK_SRC; a credential unexpectedly present that an unmodifiable runner would expose; the smoke override set; either artifact tree missing or non-empty; the allowlist differing from the twelve globs.

argument_guard.literal_source:
if [ "$#" -ne 0 ]; then
  printf 'run-opengrep.sh: takes no arguments (configuration is baked in); refusing to scan\n' >&2
  exit 64
fi
argument_guard.rejection_probe_reason: Not needed and not permitted: inspection established that the guard is the first executable statement, ahead of sourcing, target resolution and the tool call. A blind probe against a defective runner could perform a real scan and contaminate the artifact tree.

opengrep.scan_target_resolution: Indirect. The runner never names SPARK_SRC; it sources harness/lib/scope.sh at line 16 and calls scope_resolve_target at line 26, and that function reads SPARK_SRC at harness/lib/scope.sh lines 29-32 (after checking the HARNESS_SMOKE_TARGET override at line 23) and exports SCAN_ROOT and SCAN_ROOT_SOURCE.

invocation_form.target_passing_style: many paths, root-relative, in one invocation
invocation_form.targets: ${DIRS[@]} is the 18-element root-relative allowlist expansion from scope_dirs, read at line 40 and required non-empty at line 41.
invocation_form.config_arguments: ${CFG[@]} is built at lines 32-37, one --config per rule-bearing top-level directory of $OPENGREP_RULES_DIR, skipping dot-directories, stats, libsonnet and template*. Pointing --config at the ruleset root fails with InvalidRuleSchemaError on non-rule YAML, which is why the loop exists.

working_directory.note: The runner's own comment at lines 48-49 states the reason: SARIF paths are relative to the working directory, so it runs from the scan root and passes root-relative directories. This provisioning does NOT cd into the ruleset directory, so cwd and the path base coincide.

path_base.evidence: Established from the invocation and the working directory, not from any artifact: the runner cds to $SCAN_ROOT at line 50 and passes root-relative target directories, so every SARIF locations[].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri is root-relative. harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 9 independently records 'uri is root-relative to $SPARK_SRC ... Every uri was verified to exist under $SPARK_SRC; zero absolute URIs'.
path_base.sarif_resolution_note: The engine sets uriBaseId '%SRCROOT%' on every result but emits no run.originalUriBaseIds, so the SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.4 resolution procedure cannot complete. This metadata therefore supplies the explicit base above, which is the condition under which the documented degenerate-base fallback applies; without it every SARIF row would have to be rejected under unresolvable_path.

opengrep.jdk_major_evidence: No JVM is involved. file(1) reports /opt/blitzy-tools/bin/opengrep as 'ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, dynamically linked', the runner exports no JAVA_HOME, and harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 8 lists this runner as a standalone binary.
opengrep.interpreter_evidence: Not a Python-hosted tool. The PATH entry is a native ELF executable rather than a script with an interpreter shebang, and the runner invokes no interpreter.

The flag is marked internal by the tool, which is accepted at a pinned version.
opengrep scan has no --metrics flag; passing one errors with 'unknown option'. Semgrep does. The two runners' flag sets are deliberately not copies of each other.
No flag in this set appears in the AAP expected-values table, so none is an anchor. It is recorded as read; nothing was added, removed or forced.

The unsafe ${VAR:+set}${VAR:-absent} form, whose :- arm would expand to the variable's own value into a log this pipeline preserves verbatim, is not used here or anywhere in this harness.

Both values are recorded here; the expected-values table governs the field, so the difference stands as a difference.

datadog-static-analyzer.not_comparable_reason: The ruleset digest differs from the expected identity. A different rule set produces a different count for reasons that have nothing to do with the code, so this tool's finding count must not be compared against the rehearsal's figure even though the ruleset and rule counts match.

gitleaks.scan_target_resolution: Indirect, via harness/lib/scope.sh sourced at line 23 and scope_resolve_target called at line 33, which reads SPARK_SRC at harness/lib/scope.sh lines 29-32.

invocation_form.target_passing_style: exactly one root-relative path per invocation, one invocation per scope directory
invocation_form.targets: One iteration per element of the 18-directory allowlist expansion, each passed as a single root-relative path.
invocation_form.why_one_path_per_invocation: gitleaks dir takes exactly one path and silently falls back to the working directory when handed more, which would make the path base non-obvious and the reported paths wrong. The runner's header at lines 4-7 states this and the per-directory loop is the consequence. This provisioning therefore does NOT pass all eighteen paths to a single invocation.

working_directory.note: Load-bearing: because each invocation receives one root-relative path from the scan root, every reported File value is root-relative. The runner states the base itself at line 42.

path_base.evidence: From the invocation and the working directory, not from the artifact: cwd is $SCAN_ROOT (line 47) and each invocation is handed exactly one root-relative directory (line 53), so the File field of every record is root-relative to the scan root. The runner prints 'path base : <root> (root-relative paths; cwd is the scan root)' at line 42, and harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 9 records 'File root-relative to $SPARK_SRC'.

gitleaks.jdk_major_evidence: No JVM. file(1) reports /opt/blitzy-tools/bin/gitleaks as 'ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, statically linked'; the runner exports no JAVA_HOME.

interpreter.evidence: The scanner itself is a native binary and uses no interpreter. The runner invokes the system python3 once, at lines 66-78, purely to concatenate the 18 per-directory JSON arrays into the single artifact; command -v python3 resolves to /usr/bin/python3, which reports Python 3.13.7. run-trivy.sh uses the same system interpreter for the same kind of merge.

notes: --redact=100 means a matched secret's value never reaches the artifact: Secret and Match come through as REDACTED. No adapter may carry a secret value into any field, and none is recorded in this document either.
--exit-code 2 fixes the leaks-found exit code, which the runner then maps deliberately - see exit_code_mapping.

A finding that resolves into a src/test tree is retained with in_scope false rather than dropped.

joern.jdk_major_evidence: Two independent readings agree. The runner sets JAVA_HOME="$JAVA_HOME_21" at line 67 and asserts that JDK is usable at line 40; and /opt/blitzy-tools/bin/joern is itself a provisioning wrapper whose body exports JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME_21:-/opt/blitzy-tools/jdk/jdk-21.0.12.1+1}" before delegating to /opt/blitzy-tools/joern-cli/joern, because Joern's own launchers would otherwise use whatever java is on PATH - which here is 17. That JDK reports 'openjdk version "21.0.12.1" 2026-08-18 LTS' - major 21, the version the pinned release documents as its tested requirement.
joern.interpreter_evidence: Not a Python-hosted tool. It is a JVM application driven by a Scala script, and the runner invokes no interpreter.

notes: SL_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARN is load-bearing: Joern's default log level floods its own artifact, and one earlier run produced a 379 MB artifact of per-method INFO lines. The raw console stream goes to the log directory and only the counted query output becomes the artifact.

The traversal bound is HARNESS_JOERN_QUERY_BOUND, read at line 36 with a default of 2000 and passed as HARNESS_SCAN_BOUND. It governs how much work each query is asked to do, never which files or modules are in scope.
No flag in this set appears in the AAP expected-values table, so none is an anchor.
baked_flags.literal_note: Token text exactly as it appears in the runner, including the script's own quoting. invocation_form.literal holds the full command line verbatim.

joern.credential_expression_evidence: This runner reports no credential state: it calls scope_cred_state nowhere and prints no credential line, because joern reads no credential. Recorded as null rather than an empty string. Its header lines 56-62 print the graph path and its resolution, the graph's byte size and sha256, the JDK, the heap, the query set with its bound, and the workspace instead.
joern.artifact_format: native JSON with a findings array
joern.artifact_assembly: The baked script writes the artifact itself (harness/lib/joern-scan.sc lines 106-121). Each finding carries query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file and line; the envelope also carries the tool version, the cpg path, the graph's method, type-declaration and file counts, and a per-query record with its bound, returned count and bound_reached flag.

reach.allowlist_use: This is the one runner whose target set is NOT derived from the allowlist: it never calls scope_dirs for targeting, and the only allowlist read is incidental - scope_begin prints the expansion's directory count in its header (harness/lib/scope.sh line 75). Its input is the graph, which was built over every JAR the build produced.
reach.walks: The whole code-property graph, not a directory tree. Six bounded structural queries run over it.

query_set.truncation_observable: Each query takes bound+1 and reports bound_reached, so truncation is observed rather than assumed (harness/lib/joern-scan.sc lines 87-93).
query_set.load_mechanism: importCpg only, at harness/lib/joern-scan.sc line 41. importCode appears nowhere in the script; it would spawn a second JVM at the same heap.
query_set.why_bounded: The runner's header and the script's own comment record that a whole-graph sweep of Joern's default 59-query bundle over a graph of this size ran 2 h 26 m wall and 9 h 35 m CPU on this class of host without finishing. Since the scanning run imposes no time limit, an unbounded sweep would not fail - it would hang and produce no dataset. The bound governs which queries run and how much traversal each does, never which files or modules are in scope.

reach.in_tool_words: 6 bounded structural queries over the whole graph, bound 2,000, bound_reached=false on all six
reach.in_tool_words_source: harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 11, 'The Joern runner's bound, proven'
reach.in_scope_note: in_scope is decided by the allowlist alone. Because every -tests artifact the build produced is in the graph input, a finding can legitimately resolve into a src/test tree; such a row is kept with in_scope false rather than dropped.

ruleset_or_feed_identity.observed_identity: 6 bounded structural queries baked into the provisioned runner
ruleset_or_feed_identity.expected_identity: the set baked into the provisioned Joern runner; the AAP expects a 58-query bundle bounded to 6 structural queries and directs that the actual baked count be read from the runner
ruleset_or_feed_identity.evidence: Read directly from harness/lib/joern-scan.sc lines 50-78, where the six Q(...) entries are declared, and line 111 where the script labels its own output '6 bounded structural queries'. Counted from the runner rather than assumed from the default bundle size.

heap_override.mechanism: The runner applies it as -J-Xmx"$HARNESS_JOERN_HEAP" at line 70 and prints it at line 60. harness/env.sh line 85 exports HARNESS_JOERN_HEAP="${HARNESS_JOERN_HEAP:-64g}", so the documented override is an environment value the runner is written to consume rather than a configuration edit.
heap_override.raise_required_evidence: The provisioned default already meets the mandated minimum of 64 GB, so no raise was necessary and none was made. This differs from the harness precedent, whose run-joern.sh defaulted JAVA_OPTS to -Xmx48g - below the minimum - and would have required one.
heap_override.direction_rule: Raising a heap is permitted and reported; lowering one produces a truncated graph whose silence cannot be told apart from a clean result. The host was proven able to commit this heap: java -Xms64g -Xmx64g -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -version exits 0 on both JDKs.
heap_override.commit_proof_source: harness/ENVIRONMENT.md section 1, heap commit proof row

joern.exit_code_mapping: The runner exits with the tool's own exit code (lines 72-76); it does not transform it. A configuration fault - a missing graph, a missing query set, an unusable JDK 21 - exits 78 through scope_fail with a diagnostic naming the fault, which is a fault to correct rather than a scanning outcome to classify.
